text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Democratic Party of the Left (PDS) leader Massimo D'Alema said he was confident the majority was very strong after meeting Prime Minister Romano Prodi for talks on welfare state reform and Italy's entry in the first wave of European Monetary Union (all).

* The board of state industrial holding IRI said it had approved a defence alliance between its unit Finmeccanica and Britain's General Electrics Co Plc. Finmeccanica and GEC will set up a defence systems joint venture and take minority stakes in some of their respective defence operations (all).
* Italy's Antitrust authority does not approve a plan to set up of a single digital platform for satellite television services made by Rai and Stet in alliance with Mediaset and Canal Plus (all).

* Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi and Industry minister Pierluigi Bersani said latest economic figures showed the country's economy had already start to pick up and the recovery would be stable (all).
* Giorgio Fossa, the head of Italy's employers' association Confindustria, said gross domestic product growth would struggle to clear one percent this year (all).

* Motorway operator Autostrade's parent company IRI said privileged shares in Autostrade woul be converted into ordinary shares at par with no cash balance. Autostrade is due to be privatised later this summer (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
